From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Oct 3, 2024 at 9:12 AM PDT
Subject: Canary GA risk review: rollback semantics + audit log payloads (pre-GA mitigations)

Team —

As we get close to Hosted canary rollouts GA, I want to close the loop on the remaining risk items SRE/Sec flagged in the last sync:

1) Rollback/pause semantics (esp. streaming + retries)
2) Audit log payload review (PII + diff formatting + exportability)
3) Required mitigations to ship GA (validation/guardrails + alerting)

Can you reply in-thread with (a) any remaining blockers and (b) the minimum set of requirements you need for go/no-go? I’d like to freeze scope by Monday.

Current state (for reference):
- Data-plane: variant selection pinned at request start; retries should reuse selection (PR 18463)
- Control-plane: propagation race fix in flight (PR 18537)
- Audit logs: draft schema with before/after diffs implemented behind flag (PR 18509)

Attaching:
- rollout_policy_change_audit_events_v0.9.pdf
- hosted-rollout-pause-and-rollback-runbook_draft.md

Thanks,
Dylan

—
Dylan Brooks
Engineering Lead, Console
Redwood Inference


From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Oct 3, 2024 at 11:02 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Canary GA risk review: rollback semantics + audit log payloads (pre-GA mitigations)

SRE POV — not a blocker, but we need a couple items explicitly defined + tested.

Rollback / pause semantics (what we need documented + enforced):
- “Pause rollout” must mean candidate weight = 0% immediately for NEW requests once policy propagates.
- In-flight streaming requests:
  - Must NOT switch variants mid-stream.
  - If the stream fails and the client retries (same request id), selection must be stable (baseline vs candidate) to avoid mixed output + confusing comparisons.
- “Rollback” should be a named action that sets baseline=100%, candidate=0% AND marks rollout terminal (i.e., no more schedule progression).

Mitigation requirements before GA:
- Propagation staleness SLO + alerting: we need confidence that a pause/rollback reaches all Hosted regions quickly.
  - Proposed: P99 policy propagation to data-plane < 60s; page if > 5m for any region.
- A runbook that maps “Customer says errors spiked after weight change” → exact steps to force 0% candidate and verify.
- We should have at least one staging failure-injection test that simulates partial region staleness + confirms safe behavior.

If PR 18537 is in and we have dashboards + alerts linked from the runbook, I’m good.

Sean

—
Sean Gallagher
SRE Lead
Redwood Inference


From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Oct 3, 2024 at 1:18 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Canary GA risk review: rollback semantics + audit log payloads (pre-GA mitigations)

Security review notes (audit logging):

Primary concern is avoiding payload content and other customer data. The audit trail is for “who changed routing policy and what changed,” not for logging prompt/response data.

Minimum requirements for GA audit events:
- Event types: rollout.create, rollout.update, rollout.pause, rollout.rollback
- Actor attribution: user_id, org_id, (if via API) api_key_id / token_id; include “impersonated by support” field if applicable.
- Target identifiers: route_id, rollout_id, policy_version (monotonic)
- Change summary:
  - Before/after must be a structured diff of the policy object (weights, schedule steps, guardrail thresholds), BUT:
    - No freeform notes copied from UI if they can contain customer text.
    - No prompt sets / eval data in this stream.
    - No request headers or user messages.

Formatting/retention:
- JSON event body should be stable for SIEM export (don’t change field names per release without versioning).
- Ensure we have a schema_version field.
- Retention: confirm default retention meets our internal posture (we usually state 90d standard; longer via enterprise add-on). Kevin may have more detail.

Action requested: can you share an example audit event (sanitized) from staging once the payload is finalized?

Marcus

—
Marcus Lin
Security Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference


From: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Oct 3, 2024 at 2:07 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Canary GA risk review: rollback semantics + audit log payloads (pre-GA mitigations)

+1 to Marcus.

Two additions from audit/SIEM integration side:

1) Diff strategy
- Please avoid “raw before/after blob” only. We need either:
  a) explicit list of changed paths (e.g., $.variants.candidate.weight) + old/new values, OR
  b) a normalized object with deterministic ordering (so downstream dedupe works).
- Reason: some customers export to Splunk and rely on deterministic field ordering/paths.

2) Sensitive fields checklist
- “Sticky routing key” / hashing seed: do not log any secret seed material.
- If we include “sticky mode = request_hash(route_id + user_key)” we should not log user_key.
- If the UI allows a “description” field, we should either cap and scrub it OR exclude it from audit logs.

Retention:
- Default retention in our audit pipeline is 90 days online; export via webhook/S3 for enterprise.

If you can confirm schema_version and provide a sample event with the diff format, we can sign off.

Kevin

—
Kevin Osei
Security Engineering (Audit Logging / SIEM)
Redwood Inference


From: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Oct 4, 2024 at 9:26 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Canary GA risk review: rollback semantics + audit log payloads (pre-GA mitigations)

Adding SRE/Obs detail on “pause/rollback reaches all regions quickly”.

We’re planning:
- Metric: rollout_policy_staleness_seconds{region, route} (capped cardinality per standards)
- Alert:
  - Warning: P95 staleness > 90s for 10m
  - Page: any region P99 > 300s for 5m (ties to Sean’s note)
- Dashboard panel: “Time since latest policy version observed by data-plane” + “Effective weights by region”

One nuance: if a customer pauses and a region is partitioned, we need the UI to show partial propagation (don’t claim “paused” if 2/6 regions still serving candidate).

I’ll sync with Console on how to present that state; but GA requirement from my side is at least:
- operator can see region propagation status
- oncall can force baseline 100% + verify via dashboards

Allison

—
Allison Grant
Observability / SLOs
Redwood Inference


From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Oct 7, 2024 at 4:41 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Canary GA risk review: rollback semantics + audit log payloads (pre-GA mitigations)

Thanks all — here’s what we’ll do for GA scope, based on your requirements.

Rollback/pause semantics (committing):
- Pause:
  - Control-plane sets candidate weight=0 and schedule progression disabled (rollout remains editable).
  - Data-plane selection pinned per request start; in-flight streams never switch.
  - Retries with same request_id reuse the initial variant selection (baseline/candidate) for that request.
- Rollback:
  - Sets baseline=100, candidate=0 AND marks rollout state=rolled_back (terminal). Further schedule progression blocked.

Propagation/SRE:
- Landing PR 18537 (monotonic version checks + retries) this week.
- Allison’s staleness metric + alerts will be linked from the runbook; Console will show “propagation status by region” in the rollout activity view (at least for pause/rollback actions).

Audit logging (committing):
- Schema:
  - schema_version field
  - event types: create/update/pause/rollback
  - actor + target identifiers as Marcus requested
- Diff:
  - We’ll emit changed_paths with old/new values (no raw JSON blobs only).
- Sensitive fields:
  - No prompt/eval data.
  - No user-provided sticky key; we log only sticky_mode enum and hash strategy name (no seed/user_key).
  - Exclude freeform description from audit payload (still stored in rollout object, but not exported via audit log).

Next steps / asks:
- Kevin + Marcus: once PR 18509 is updated with changed_paths format, I’ll send a sanitized sample event from staging for final sign-off.
- Sean/Allison: please confirm the alert thresholds above are acceptable for GA, and we’ll lock them into the release checklist.

Marissa — we’ll incorporate the above into GA go/no-go criteria.

Dylan

—
Dylan Brooks
Engineering Lead, Console
Redwood Inference
